question: Can the 394 elements of the sample be written as tokens and a graph, and cut into ~20-node BFS subgraphs?
notes: One model only (Autodesk sample): this is a smoke test of the representation, not a result about learning.

Door/window -> wall and element -> level come from the JSON; wall-wall, wall-floor and room-floor are derived from geometry (tolerances 0.30 m and 0.50 m), because extract.py does not read joins or attachments.
Levels are context: subgraphs do not walk through them, so a piece stays local.
Floors are tokenised as their bounding box and area: L-shaped outlines cannot be rebuilt from the tokens.
Door and window size is carried by the type token, not by separate size bins.
Rooms are only a point and an area: no boundaries, no adjacency between rooms.
Subgraphs start at every element, so they overlap; unique_subgraphs counts distinct node sets.
The 20 elements outside the largest component are walls on the Roof level (parapets): roofs are not extracted, so nothing joins them to the rest.
Subgraphs cross levels (levels_per_subgraph_mean): exterior walls run from the entry level to the roof and touch every slab on the way.
Bins lose position: at 0.50 m the mean error is 0.22 m, never within 1 cm. Placing a prediction for the 1 cm comparison needs the exact host wall line, not the bin centre.
